To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the traditional approach of relating each image to a single abstract coordinate system may not be appropriate for some tasks and that a hierarchical framework for representing scenes is a useful approach.
Representing a scene as a collection of images rather than as a set of three dimensional coordinates has a number of practical advantages.

a hierarchical representation of images that directly represents the relationships between the images can be used to solve a number of important vision problems and that these relationships can be computed in a practical and efficient manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a representation of the information derived from a set of images and with algorithms that can compute this representation.
the development of algorithms and representations for computer vision that are more directly based on the collection of images.
the development of a new approach to the representation of scenes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approach to scene representation presented here has many practical advantages.
a representation based on relationships between the collection of images is more appropriate than the traditional approach based on a single three dimensional coordinate system.
the representation of information about a scene by relating each image in a collection to an abstract three-dimensional coordinate system may not be appropriate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new representation for scenes and the algorithms to compute them.
we have developed an approach to representing the relationships among a collection of images.
we have developed a hierarchical representation for scenes, which is more compact than previous representations, and is more efficient for many applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a hierarchical representation of a scene is more useful than a single representation of the scene.
the traditional representation of information about the world by relating each image in the scene to a three dimensional coordinate system does not always provide the most useful information.
the representation of scenes is not a single, static entity but is a dynamic process that changes with time as new images are collected and the scene is explored.
